Looking at the 13C NMR spectrum, I can identify the aromatic carbons by their chemical shifts. According to the reference data, aromatic carbons (Ar-C and Ar-H) typically appear between 115-150 ppm, with some substituted aromatic carbons appearing up to about 160 ppm.

In the spectrum, we see peaks at:
- 161.40 ppm (aromatic carbon with electron-withdrawing substituent)
- 143.85 ppm (aromatic carbon)
- 130.30 ppm (aromatic carbon)

The other peaks (26.65, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20 ppm) are in the aliphatic region.

Therefore, there are 3 aromatic carbons in the molecule.
